long_biography.plain_text:
Graham Gilkison and his wife Kim bought a struggling vineyard on Paewhenua Island near Mangonui. The vines needed heavy pruning, reorganisation and substantial new planting. Working with local vineyard managers and staff, the couple restored production and adopted sustainability measures covering soil health, recycling and the surrounding wetland. Their winery now makes Northland wines and welcomes visitors to an on-site tasting room.

Before the move into viticulture, Gilkison was among the owners of ITL, a New Plymouth process and mechanical engineering business serving energy and pipeline projects. The consultancy employed engineers and designers and supplied clients in New Zealand and overseas. The couple sold their engineering business before developing the winery, bringing an established operating-business background to a different kind of production. The vineyard's restoration earned a regional agri-business management award, and the family remains involved in its wine operation.
